findings.text: the tree-derived aperture's verdict has no test that fails if it is deleted, so five lines of editing turn the new requirement back into a count with nothing verified: the fixture at line 325 sits inside a configured root and its default is an empty container, so the roots loop at line 215 reaches the same violation and the file stays green under the deletion (probe log). Triggering input: delete lines 241-245, leave lines 237-240 counting, and run the file — 6 passed. A fixture placed outside every configured root with an empty-container default is reported today, which is the test that closes this, and it is the only shape that distinguishes the two apertures.

MODULE_ROOTS still carries the requirement for every literal-name defaulted read that is not an empty-container default, so the bypass the previous review measured on this file still reproduces: substituting one root for another whose reads are all declared leaves the file at 6 passed while the dropped module's three candidates go unchecked. Triggering input: replace imas_codex/standard_names/export.py in MODULE_ROOTS with a root whose literal reads all resolve, and run the file — 6 passed (probe_substitution_declared_names.log).

the candidate floor names the literal-name class over the roots but is now compared against the union of both apertures, measured 60 (30 roots plus 30 empty-container, intersection 0), so all 30 of the roots' candidates could go unchecked without moving this number. Triggering input: drop one root's candidates by editing that root's reads to a computed name and, at the same time, grow any empty-container read by one — the floor stays green while the roots' requirement has shrunk.

the exemption dict is keyed by attribute name alone and applies package-wide, so a future in-package miss of the same attribute name is excused silently: the entry was added for a foreign LinkML slot at imas_codex/graph/schema.py:406, but nothing ties it to that receiver, and the scan never inspects a receiver at all. Triggering input, measured: one added entry turns getattr(subject, "phantom_field", []) in imas_codex/graph/lookalike.py from a reported violation into no violation while the committed counterexample assertions still hold, and the same-name read stays exempt in an unrelated subtree, so the entry cannot distinguish the foreign slot from an in-package class field (probe_exemption_aperture.log).

Independent review of r-20260921T124129677197-n-the-guarded-surface-is-derived-from-the-tree
(imas-codex, plan sn-lifecycle-integrity), base 3c55df8a188169cc03bce63e18468078d5e91c93,
reviewed tip 697b1604dd5081486beba3b09fcc72f69349e6ae. Read the node's dispatch goal and
done_when, its manifest, both commits commit by commit, the test file at the tip, the six logs
the manifest names, and one probe of my own.

Is this version different in kind from the previous three? For the surface it now derives, yes:
the empty-container surface is not enumerated at all, so there is nothing inside the file to
edit that can uncover a module of that shape — a substitution cannot shrink it. For the file's
whole requirement it is not: line 20 still enumerates MODULE_ROOTS, which is what decides
whether a literal-name defaulted read whose default is not an empty container must resolve.
The previous review's substitution still reproduces against that half of the requirement.

ONE. Cheapest edit that shrinks the guarded surface with no test failing: one added line at
tests/standard_names/test_defaulted_attributes_exist.py:30, a fourth entry in
LEGITIMATELY_ABSENT_DEFAULTED_ATTRIBUTES — measured, one added entry turns a real violation
(imas_codex/graph/lookalike.py:1:phantom_field) into no violation while every committed
assertion in the file still holds (probe_exemption_aperture.log). Five lines at 241-245 are the
same class by a different route: deleting the violation check in the tree-derived loop leaves
the counts at 237-240 intact, both floors hold and the committed counterexample still reports,
so the file stays at 6 passed with the derived verdict gone (probe_verdict_branch_coverage.log).
What blocks what: DELETION of a configured root is blocked by the module floor at line 270 and
the per-root assertions at lines 283-288 (the node's own second control log reds at "scanned 10
modules, below the ratchet floor of 11"); SUBSTITUTION is blocked for the tree-derived surface
(nothing to enumerate) but NOT for the roots surface, where a count-preserving swap whose
substitute reads only declared names stays green (the node's probe_substitution_declared_names.log
records 6 passed); SILENT NARROWING of the derived surface is blocked only by the counts, so
narrowing that keeps the counts passes; and ADDING AN EXEMPTION is not blocked at all — one line,
package-wide effect, no assertion anywhere that an entry other than the fixture's own name is
justified.

TWO. The census was re-derived independently: a byte-level regex over imas_codex, not the
node's AST walk, finds 30 calls in 9 modules, and the same regex restricted to the three
previously declared roots finds 0 — the disjointness the node reports holds, and it is what
makes the derivation meaningful, since the surface the guard had before covered none of the
shape it now requires. The nine modules sit in four distinct subtrees (graph, standard_names
including fanout, discovery/base, services), so any narrowing of SOURCE_PACKAGE to a proper
sub-path drops at least one module and trips the 9-module floor: the walk's root is
floor-protected in both directions, which is the one thing the floors do buy.

THREE. The exemption's justification is correct as far as it goes: imas_codex/graph/schema.py:406
reads annotations off a LinkML SlotDefinition (slot), a foreign object whose annotations are
linkml-runtime metadata, so the receiver is genuinely outside this package. Two things are
measured against the entry itself. Good: it is load-bearing — deleting it from the dict makes
the same read report as a violation, so the entry cannot be quietly removed. Not good: it is
keyed by attribute name alone and the scan never looks at a receiver, so the same name in a
module unrelated to LinkML is exempt by the same rule (measured, in another subtree), and one
added entry is enough to excuse any name anywhere in the package. Nothing in the file ties the
entry to the slot it was written for.

FOUR. The floors still add something only where counts move: the module floor at line 270 is the
one that refuses a root deletion. As they stand they are mismatched in both directions:
MINIMUM_EMPTY_CONTAINER_MODULES and MINIMUM_EMPTY_CONTAINER_GETATTRS sit exactly at the measured
9 and 30, so the first legitimate shrink of the tree is a spurious red whose message tells the
reader never to lower it; MINIMUM_LITERAL_DEFAULTED_GETATTRS stays 30 while the quantity it is
compared against is now the union of both apertures, 60 measured, so half of what the message
claims it measures can vanish without moving it.
